tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when...'), focuses on user intent with concrete trigger phrases users might say, and covers scope explicitly including implicit contexts (unexpected cost increases, expensive protection plans). It is a single dense paragraph, which is on the longer side but still concise enough to convey scope without excessive verbosity.
tests.evidence: Use this skill when a user asks to reduce, review, audit, or optimize GuardDuty spend, or reports an unexpected GuardDuty cost increase or an expensive protection plan. Activate on requests like "why is my GuardDuty bill so high", "reduce GuardDuty costs"...

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body is concise and focuses on GuardDuty-specific billing mechanics, non-obvious behaviors (Runtime Monitoring offsetting VPC Flow Logs), and procedural steps rather than explaining general AWS/cost concepts the agent already knows.
tests.evidence: Runtime Monitoring offsets VPC Flow Log charges — for instances the Runtime Monitoring agent covers, GuardDuty stops charging for VPC Flow Log processing.

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: Detailed reference data (per-plan metric tables, API call specifics, opportunity check definitions) is explicitly offloaded to references/ files rather than embedded in the body, even within conditional workflow steps.
tests.evidence: For the full per-plan metric/unit/pricing table, the two critical billing behaviors, and byte-to-GB/TB conversions, load [references/billing-model.md](references/billing-model.md)

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: All three reference files are linked via markdown links in the body.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link is accompanied by a specific trigger condition for when to load it.
tests.evidence: load [references/data-collection.md](references/data-collection.md) when identifying which plan drives a charge or reasoning about the Runtime Monitoring offset.

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths from the skill root with no traversal or absolute paths.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile operations (read-only API boundaries, validation checks, severity SLAs) are prescriptive and exact, while analysis/reasoning steps (e.g., how to weigh cost vs security value) give the agent explanatory freedom.
tests.evidence: Frame every recommendation against security value — never recommend disabling a plan purely on cost.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: The skill doesn't present competing tool options as equal menus; it specifies a clear preferred signal (Cost Explorer) with a fallback.
tests.evidence: prefer Cost Explorer as the dollar signal, reconciled against the usage metrics. ... If neither Cost Explorer nor usage metrics are available, still report configuration findings

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The workflow teaches a generalizable procedure (scope identification, inventory, metric collection, opportunity analysis, validation, reporting) applicable to any GuardDuty cost review, not a one-off instance.
tests.evidence: Step 1: Identify target scope. Ask the user which accounts and Regions to review...

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: A dedicated Known Quirks section documents concrete, non-obvious environment-specific facts the agent would otherwise get wrong.
tests.evidence: Your own log configuration does not change GuardDuty cost — do not recommend turning off customer VPC Flow Logs, CloudTrail, or S3 data events to reduce GuardDuty spend

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: The skill produces a report and provides an explicit template asset for it.
tests.evidence: Load that template when generating the report. ... assets/report-template.md

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body
tests.reasoning: No large inline template exists in the body; the report structure is instead delegated to assets/report-template.md.
tests.evidence: Produce a shareable Markdown report artifact following the structure, section order, and table schemas in [assets/report-template.md](assets/report-template.md).

tests.name: Asset files must be linked
tests.reasoning: The single asset file is referenced in the body.
tests.evidence: [assets/report-template.md](assets/report-template.md). Load that template when generating the report.

tests.name: Asset links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: The asset reference specifies exactly when to load it (during report generation).
tests.evidence: Load that template when generating the report.

tests.name: Asset path format
tests.reasoning: The asset link uses a relative path from the skill root.

tests.name: Step-by-step guidance
tests.reasoning: The procedural workflow is presented as an ordered checkbox checklist with 'Step N' labeling as required.

tests.name: Validation loops
tests.reasoning: Step 5 explicitly instructs the agent to self-check its findings for correctness before producing the final report.
tests.evidence: Step 5: Validate findings. Before writing the report, self-check the findings: confirm estimated savings sum correctly and each traces to a cited metric or cost signal...
